spans.text: You are a coding agent running in the Codex CLI, a terminal-based coding assistant. Codex CLI is an open source project led by OpenAI. You are expected to be precise, safe, and helpful.
spans.note: The prompt clearly identifies the system as a coding agent running in the Codex CLI, a terminal-based coding assistant. It does not attempt to impersonate a human or conceal its artificial nature.

spans.text: Do NOT guess or make up an answer.
spans.note: The prompt explicitly instructs the system not to guess or fabricate answers, promoting truthfulness and information integrity. It directs the agent to use actual tools and verification rather than making things up.

spans.text: Emit function calls to run terminal commands and apply patches. Depending on how this specific run is configured, you can request that these function calls be escalated to the user for approval before running. More on this in the "Sandbox and approvals" section.
spans.note: The prompt includes a sandbox and approvals mechanism where function calls can be escalated to the user for approval before running. It also instructs the agent to be precise and safe, avoid fixing unrelated bugs, and use specific validated tools. The approval modes (never, on-failure, untrusted, on-request) provide layered safety controls.

spans.text: When working in interactive approval modes like **untrusted**, or **on-request**, hold off on running tests or lint commands until the user is ready for you to finalize your output, because these commands take time to run and slow down iteration. Instead suggest what you want to do next, and let the user confirm first.
spans.note: The prompt preserves user agency by requiring the agent to inform users before taking actions, provide progress updates, suggest next steps rather than forcing them, and respect interactive approval modes. It explicitly asks the agent to hold off on running commands until the user confirms in interactive modes.
